actions.action: Push a finger or skewer 3–4 inches into the soil to check moisture
Water the plant if the soil is dry throughout
Lift the plant out of the pot to inspect the roots for rot and root-binding
If roots are mushy, trim them and repot in fresh well-draining soil
If root-bound, repot into a slightly larger pot
Water when the top inch is barely dry and let excess drain fully
Use filtered, distilled, or rainwater instead of hard tap water
Let tap water sit out overnight before using
Run a humidifier near the plant during the day
Set up a pebble tray under the plant
Group the plant with other plants for humidity
Move the plant to bright indirect light away from vents, drafts and temperature swings
Trim fully brown leaves and crispy edges following the leaf shape

reason: The answer names water stress but hedges between underwatering and overwatering/root rot, and misses the broken stems. Watering if the soil is dry deeper down is present but buried behind root checks and humidity advice. Nothing recommended is likely to harm the plant.
